title: Ops Curator — Contextual Remediator Hub and Heuristic Hooks
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: On-call engineers and support agents repeatedly execute short, structured remediation steps (e.g., cache clears, service restarts, routing toggles), but creating, discovering, and safely invoking those actions is slow and error-prone. Current runbooks are long human-readable docs; we need a lightweight, typed surface for small, safe automations that can be recommended by telemetry and executed with permissions and audit.

Proposal: Build an "ops curator" service (remediator hub) that publishes a catalog of small, idempotent remediation 'execlets' (atomic tasklets). Execlets are metadata-first: typed inputs, preconditions (SLO/metric predicates), safety gates, required roles, and simulated dry-run output. The hub exposes: (1) a discovery API for contextual suggestions (based on current alert, traces, and metric patterns), (2) an interactive console surface for technicians to run execlets with forced dry-run and preview modes, and (3) an execution API used by automated responders and playflow engines.

Design constraints and differentiators: execlets must be small (<= 6 steps), reversible or have compensating actions where applicable, and explicitly idempotent. Telemetry suggestions should be probabilistic and require human confirmation for any execlet that has side-effects above a threshold. All executions are audited, tainted traces are stored for postmortem, and canary policies control automated invocation.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement a full-playbook compiler or AI-suggested full remediation flows. It focuses on catalog, discovery, safety gating, and the first ~15 execlets for common support tasks.

Acceptance criteria below enumerate functional checks, rollout criteria, and the data/telemetry hooks required.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog service implemented: REST endpoints to list execlets, view metadata, and query by tag/alert signature.
Execlet schema validated: typed inputs, precondition predicates, estimated impact, required roles, and dry-run handler.
Console surface wireframe + MVP integration: operators can preview, dry-run, and execute execlets with prompting and 2-step confirmation for high-impact actions.
Telemetry integration: recommendations surface from alerts/metric-signatures (basic rule engine) and includes confidence score and rationale link.
Audit trail: every execlet invocation creates an immutable audit event (user, inputs, timestamp, diff snapshot link) visible in the Console timeline.
Safety gates: execlets with potential cross-customer impact require 'escalation' role and cannot be run by default on shared Dedicated clusters.
15 initial execlets implemented and smoke-tested in staging with synthetic incidents (see implementation_steps for list).
Automated test harness that runs execlet dry-run handlers and verifies idempotency via state-compare snapshots.
implementation_steps: Define execlet manifest schema (YAML/JSON schema) and register in code repo — include fields: id, title, tags, inputs, preconditions, impact_level, roles, dry_run_hint, compensating_action.
Build lightweight catalog service (Go) with DB table for execlet manifests + simple ACL check for roles.
Add discovery API that accepts alert context (alert_id, metric_snapshot, trace_id) and returns ranked execlet candidates with confidence and rationale.
Console UI: embed suggestion drawer and execution modal with dry-run preview and required confirmation UX. Work with Design for microcopy (see links).
Implement execlet runtime shim that can run dry-run handlers and real handlers behind feature-flagged endpoints; include sandbox mode for staging runbook validation.
Create 15 seed execlets for common ops tasks (cache-clear, service-rotate, node-cordon/uncordon with drain safety, config-toggle-with-rollback), add tests.
Wire audit events into existing telemetry pipeline (trace, SLO tags, Grafana dashboard panel) and add a per-execlet latency/impact card.
Run staged canary: roll out to internal-only workspace, shadow automated suggestions, collect false-positive/false-negative telemetry for two weeks, iterate thresholds.
